content: I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!

A similar clash exists: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/412346134688c581887a301794e266753d529
IMO this problem is too difficult to be a clash of code.

Goal
* Please format "0" (2 instances) and "1" as {{constants}}.

Input
* Please format "0" and "1" as {{constants}}.

Constraints
* Please change "|S|" to "length of [[S]]".

* Please change 200000 to 10 as the length never exceeds 10.

Stub generator
* Please change 200000 to 10.

* Please add a write statement.

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario with slightly different inputs. So,

  - Please revise Validator 4 so that the longest balanced segment excludes the starting and ending digits.

  - Please use the original Validator 4 as Test 5, and create a similar case (the longest balanced segment excludes the starting digits) to be Validator 5.

  - Please create Test 6 and Validator 6 where the longest balanced segment excludes the ending digits.

  - Please create Test 7 and Validator 7 where the length of [[S]] is odd and the output is greater than 0.

  - Please create Test 8 and Validator 8 where the length of [[S]] = 1.

Thanks.

Stub generator
* Please change line 2 to "write answer".

Cases
* Too many test inputs start with 0 and validator inputs start with 1. Please:
  - swap Test 2 and Validator 2.
  - swap Test 3 and Validator 3.

* Some scenarios I mentioned previously haven't been covered. Please add:
  - Test 8: 1111110001
  - Validator 8: 0000001110
  - Test 9: 1000111111
  - Validator 9: 0111000000

Thanks.

Granted the author tests set is not satisfying.
But I disagree on the difficulty remark as an easy and naive brute force is a mere handful of lines of python and way easier than many clashes I saw.
Plus, the referenced similar clash is a bit more costly as it additionally requires solving balanced parens (vs merely counting '0' and '1' here).
I must say I find your feedback strange considering how involved(!) your clash proposals are :D.

If the intended way is to brute-force a solution, then sure. But seeing as the author has set the constraints of the length of string S to be a large number, and after reviewing the author's solution, I can only assume (as the author has not yet replied to @5DN1L's comment) that brute force might not be enough.

I agree with you on the balanced parentheses problem being slightly more "costly". Not sure if it makes the code any more complicated, but it does introduce more constraints to think about.

Also in my defence I would say my clashes tend to only involve string manipulation or more unconventional thinking. I try not to introduce "advanced" concepts such as BFS/DFS, prefix sums, or dynamic programming (ok except the LCIS one). Clashes that rely on such techniques I would generally consider "too difficult". Feel free to disagree though haha :p

I would see some benefit in having some 'hard to 100% top' clashes where the missing % are not merely a ~useless corner case.
However I overlooked the points you are mentioning, the author's constraints and solution, and I better understand your point now.
